summary: Lyra Insurance: intermittent tokenization failures causing degraded embeddings throughput and cascading 5xx errors
description:
Issue summary:
Between 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC and 2026-03-10 06:10 UTC Lyra Insurance observed intermittent failures for embedding requests that used Redwood's embedding endpoints. Errors manifested as 500/502 responses and stalled streaming for a subset of customer requests. The root trigger was a tokenizer component regression causing certain outlier input batches (multi-line policy documents with mixed encodings) to throw exceptions during tokenization.

Impact:
- ~18% of Lyra production embedding calls failed with 5xx for a 2.5 hour window.
- End-to-end embedding throughput for Lyra (dedicated pool) dropped by ~60% leading to request queueing and higher tail latency for other customers using the same Dedicated pool.
- Autoscaler reacted to apparent latency by rapidly adding and removing workers, causing increased GPU churn and billing anomalies for Lyra's reserved capacity.
- Customer reported increased errors visible in their app, automated retries led to duplicate events.

Initial detection:
- Lyra Support engineer opened a ticket and escalated to Redwood via priority channel.
- Alerts fired from per-customer error-rate dashboards and dedicated-pool SLO monitors.

Expected behavior:
Embedding requests for supported models should not fail tokenization for inputs that previously succeeded; dedicated pools should isolate CPU-level tokenizer failures and not cascade to whole-pool throughput degradation.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer payload: multi-line policy document with mixed UTF-8 and legacy Windows-1252 punctuation (example provided in ticket).
2) POST to /v1/embeddings with model=openlm-embed-1024-v2 and batch size 8.
3) Observe request sometimes returns 502 or times out; reproduced more often when inputs include long contiguous sequences of non-standard whitespace and soft-hyphen characters.
4) Repro rate ~20% in Lyra's sample corpus, not deterministic in small synthetic sets.
logs_snippets:
[2026-03-10T03:48:17Z] tokenizer-service.ERROR tokenization_exception input_index=3 error=UnicodeDecodeError('utf-8', b'\x96', 0, 1, 'invalid start byte')
[2026-03-10T03:49:02Z] serving-runtime.WARNING backpressure queue_size=312 pool_id=ded-pool-07
[2026-03-10T03:50:11Z] autoscaler.INFO scale_event add_workers=3 pool=ded-pool-07 reason=high_tail_latency
[2026-03-10T05:05:22Z] gateway.ERROR upstream-502 model=openlm-embed-1024-v2 request_id=rb-9f3b4
investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis 1: tokenizer library update (rev 2.1.4 -> 2.2.0) introduced stricter decoding behavior for non-UTF inputs.
- Hypothesis 2: Batch pre-processing path bypassed fallback sanitizer for dedicated-pool traffic under high concurrency.
- Correlation: Tokenizer errors spike aligns with commit github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer@2.2.0 merged 2026-03-09 and deployment window 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC.
- Reproduced locally by feeding mixed-encoding snippets into tokenizer-service running 2.2.0; downgrade to 2.1.4 eliminated exception.
- Observed autoscaler thrash: short-lived latency spikes from tokenizer exceptions caused scale-up decisions; scale down occurred before workers processed cached warmup leading to oscillation.
- Customer tenancy isolation: Lyra was on a shared Dedicated pool (configuration gap) instead of a fully isolated pool; follow-up check flagged misconfiguration on account settings.
- Link to Slack thread: #support-lyra (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C04S2KJ1H), SRE postmortem draft link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/INC-2026-0310-01
resolution:
Mitigation performed 2026-03-10 04:10 UTC:
1) Rolled back tokenizer library on serving nodes from 2.2.0 -> 2.1.4 for affected Dedicated pool.
2) Applied on-the-fly input sanitizer that normalizes legacy encodings to UTF-8 at the gateway for Lyra's tenant requests.
3) Temporarily increased min_workers for ded-pool-07 to provide capacity and disabled aggressive scale-down cooldowns.
4) Pinning: Lyra's account temporarily pinned to model-version=openlm-embed-1024-v2@2026-03-08 to avoid newer integration paths.
5) Issued customer credit for excess autoscaler-driven usage and for failed requests (billing team notified).

Permanent fix deployed 2026-03-12 14:20 UTC:
- Tokenizer library patched to safely decode mixed encodings with a fallback sanitizer and added unit tests covering legacy punctuation. Patch merged and deployed via PR github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer/pull/56.
- Account configuration change: Lyra moved to an isolated dedicated pool per enterprise contract to avoid cross-tenant CPU failure impact.
- Autoscaler policy updated to incorporate tokenizer-exception-aware signals to avoid oscillation.
resolution_notes:
- Verify: Post-deploy SLO checks show error-rate for Lyra at <0.1% for embeddings and stable throughput.
- Customer acceptance: Lyra confirmed in Slack that their bulk ingestion job completed successfully after fixes.
- Billing: Finance applied one-week credit and will follow-up with an itemized breakdown.
- Post-incident actions recorded: create account-config validation rule, add tokenizer regression tests to CI gate, update dedicated-pool runbook.
- Owner for follow-ups: Marco Diaz (serving runtime) and Priya Nair (customer success).
